title: Multiwave activation steward timeline and safety contracts (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a multiwave activation steward timeline + safety contracts framework tailored to cross-functional LLM feature rollouts. Intent is practical — give stewards a minimal checklist, explicit tickets/escapes, and quantitative safety gates that can be simulated before any real traffic exposure.

Audience:
- Activation stewards (oncall/rotation)
- Product PMs and Eng leads running the rollout
- Observability/SRE and Solutions Eng for fallbacks and capacity

High-level objectives (short):
- Make the steward role actionable: concrete timeboxes, who calls the rollbacks, and where signals live.
- Define safety contracts that combine behavioral quality, latency, and cost to determine go/no-go per wave.
- Provide a compact simulation recipe teams can run locally/on staging to estimate false-positive/negative gating rates.

Quick glossary (team shorthand):
- steward = person responsible for rollout watch & final decision during wave (not necessarily code owner).
- wave = discrete exposure increment (e.g., 1% → 5% → 20% → 100%).
- probe traffic = synthetic/controlled requests sent to replicate vulnerable slices.
- fallback = immediate traffic switch to baseline model + alert to oncall.

Activation steward timeline (template for a single wave)
- T-minus 48h: Preflight sync (steward, PM, SRE, data-science). Confirm runbook links, monitoring dashboards, synthetic probes, escalation list (phone tree).
- T-minus 24h: Run smoke probe suite against canary image; record outputs and sample traces. Attach artifacts to JIRA INF-2768.
- T-minus 4h: Canary config bake: traffic slices, quota, burst policy, route priorities. Confirm fallback route in infra.
- T-minus 15m: Final stakeholder ping (email + slack @oncall). Activate monitoring hooks (higher retention for this wave).
- Wave start (0m): Release slice to X% traffic. Steward posts start time and unique wave-id in #launch-coordination.
- +30m: First pass check: steady-state latency P50/P95, user-facing error rate, key QA prompts sampled.
- +90m: Deeper checkpoint: model-level quality metrics on production prompts (approx), metric drift detector, and cost burn-rate.
- Gate decision window ends at +180m unless steward extends. If all gates green, proceed to next wave or end.

Decision authority and escalation:
- Steward has unilateral authority to pause or revert wave. Reversion steps are documented in infra runbook (GH PR #72).
- If revert is executed, steward files a postmortem stub in INF-2768 within 24h and notifies product and sales.

Safety contracts (composite gating rules)
- Behavioral quality (BQ): Compare top-k rerank score drift and a small human-labeled sample (N=50). Gate pass if: mean top-1 semantic similarity delta <= 0.06 and human sample pass rate >= 88%.
- Latency contract (LC): P95 latency relative increase <= 30% AND absolute P95 <= 750ms. If P95 > 1s, automatic soft-fallback (route 30%→baseline).
- Cost/throughput contract (CC): Token burn-rate should not exceed predicted model forecast by >40% over 60m window. If overrun persists 30m, steward must approve additional burst capacity or rollback.
- Composite rule: wave proceeds only if >=2 of 3 contracts are green and the third is not critical (e.g., latency > threshold triggers immediate revert).

Signal definitions and concrete thresholds (examples)
- User-facing error rate: 5xx + model error signals < 0.2% in 30m sliding window. Threshold: 0.5% escalation.
- Semantic drift probe: embedding cosine mean shift < 0.06 over 10k requests.
- Toxicity/regression checks: negative sentiment increase < 1.5x baseline on sampled prompts.
- Coverage hit rate (for cache): cache hit >= 18% for conversational flows otherwise expect ~30% on steady-state.

Simulation recipe (quick) — to estimate gate sensitivity before rollout:
- Inputs: historical request sample (N=40k), baseline model traces, proposed model traces.
- Perturbations: add simulated long-context requests (5–10% of sample), adversarial prompts (2%), and high-rate burst windows (1% of timeline).
- Run Monte Carlo (100 runs) and measure fraction of runs where any contract would trigger rollback. Aim for < 10% false-positive rollbacks in simulation.
- Notes: this is intentionally biased conservative; lower tolerance for consumer-facing product launches.

Practical traffic slice examples (do not copy exact weights without product signoff)
- Step A: 0.5% segmented by 5 small microcohorts (0.1% each) to validate variance across sub-slices.
- Step B: 3% split: 1% new-user cohort, 2% safe-history cohort.
- Step C: 15% mixed traffic with canary weighting 80/20 new/baseline prompts.
- Step D: Ramp to 100% in waves, only after two consecutive green 24h windows post Step C.

Communication templates (short)
- Slack start message (steward): "Starting wave {{wave-id}} → {{pct}}% at {{time}}. Dash: <url>. Watch: latency, error, semantic-drift. If revert, I will post reason + tag eng-oncall."
- Revert/postmortem stub: one-line summary, immediate cause, a minimal mitigation plan, and owner for follow-up.

Fallback patterns (order of operations)
1) Route-level fallback to baseline model (fastest path).
2) If routing fails, kill canary service instances and scale baseline.
3) If issue persists, open PagerDuty and start oncall war room.

On-call and SRE runbook pointers (quick links)
- GH runbook for traffic switching: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts/pull/72
- Infra incident playbook: confluence RW-Incident-Playbook (linked above)

Post-release telemetry checklist (what to capture)
- Full traces for a sampled 1k requests per wave stored under wave-id for 14 days.
- Human-labeled sample artifacts (N=50) uploaded to INF-2768.
- Cost ledger snapshot (tokens, raw compute minutes) and comparison to forecast.

Open questions / risks to surface (working):
- How to unify human-in-the-loop sample collection across distributed PM teams without biasing labels. (Priya to prototype a shared sampling UI)
- Do we need an automated rollback if semantic-drift detector triggers AND toxicity detector triggers within the same 10m window? (current approach keeps steward manual but we might want a fast-path)
- Can SRE provide a low-friction burst-capacity button in Redwood Console that increments by controlled steps?

Next steps (practical owners):
- Ethan: implement Monte Carlo sim harness and add to CI (due 2026-03-02).
- Priya: prototype shared sampling UI for human labels (due 2026-03-08).
- Marco: wire a lightweight dashboard that shows composite contract status per wave-id (due 2026-03-05).
- Lena: iterate this doc after first dry-run and capture lessons (due 2026-03-12).

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratchpad):
- Consider adding a small financial guardrail that halts wave if projected spend > X per customer segment (helps sales-pricing conversations).
- Add a tiny 'smell test' for hallucination: a short set of prompts with known factual answers run every 15m.
- Keep communication short and repeatable; humans ignore long messages under pressure.

Attachments to add before next preflight:
- Simulation run outputs (CSV), sample traces (traced-request-ids.txt), list of microcohorts and matching SQLs.

End of draft — please copy + paste sections into team-specific runbooks as needed.
